messages.subject: Re: Geom_map
parts:
Hi,

the workaround I am using is to plot these Bundeslands separately in later layers. Here is part of my working code:

p<-ggplot(data=subset(DE.map, hole==FALSE), aes(long,lat,fill=ind, group=group))+
  geom_polygon() +
  geom_polygon(data=subset(DE.map, NAME_1=="Bremen"))+
  geom_polygon(data=subset(DE.map, NAME_1=="Berlin"))+
  geom_path(color="white") +
  coord_map(projection="lagrange")
...


best,
Indrek


reede, 12. aprill 2013 16:12.05 UTC+8 kirjutas fri...@stat-up.com:
Hi,

I'm playing around with geom_map and I can't seem to get it working properly.

Basically if you 
1. take the Bundesland shapefiles from http://www.odbl.de/boundaries/ then 
2. use fortify to create a data.frame and 
3. plot some data

you will notice that Berlin has vanished.

I assume that's because it's surrounded by Brandenburg and the Brandenburg polygon (with a cut-out for Berlin missing) is drawn after the Berlin polygon.

Note that borders appear just fine (lines are drawn after fills?) which makes this kinda sneaky if you're not looking for it.

Am I missing something?


Thanks for any help. 
Stefan

messages.author: 33730d0de61ed699
messages.subject: Re: Geom_map
parts:
Yeah, that's what I'm doing, too.

But that only works if you've got a full list of locked-in territories. Easy with states, difficult with counties or towns. It'd even be possible to construct two regions that can't be plotted at the same time (each with an enclave of the other).

Btw. Bremen is unnecessary because Lower Saxony's got a lower id, which shows just how random and arbitrary the behavior is (from a results POV. Basically whether a territory is rendered correctly or not depends on a purely administrative number). 

Thanks a lot for your reply. =)

Stefan
